Cursed Clash

A Jujutsu Kaisen fighting game. Two sorcerers, big multi-level maps that break apart, cursed tools to fight over, and domain expansions.

The basics

  • Each fighter has 100 HP. In Normal mode you have 3 lives; lose them all and you lose the match.
  • Every character has a melee combo, two abilities on cooldowns, a super that charges as you deal damage, and a domain or ultimate that charges more slowly.
  • Almost every technique breaks the terrain. Broken terrain grows back after 30 seconds.
  • On big maps the camera zooms out to keep both fighters on screen, down to the whole map.

Account, shop & vows

Play matches to earn coins (¥), then spend them on special feats and binding vows.

Account

Open 👤 Account on the home screen. Your progress is saved in this browser. To move it to another computer, press GET MY SAVE CODE, copy the code, and on the other computer paste it into LOAD SAVE CODE. (If online accounts are ever connected, you can also create an account with an email and password so your coins, unlocks and stats follow you to any computer. Creating an account keeps everything you earned as a guest.)

Coins

Every online match you win pays ¥5 (losses pay nothing). New players start with ¥50. Local matches on one device don't earn coins — otherwise you could just farm yourself.

Gamepad

Stick or D-pad to move · A jump · X attack · LB / RB abilities · Y super · RT domain · B pick up.

Sound

All music and sound effects are generated live in the browser. There are four original pieces: a calm menu theme, a fast fight theme, an eerie domain theme while any domain is open, and a fever theme during Hakari's jackpot. Fighters call out their techniques with lines you record yourself in the Voice Lab (home screen): record each line with your mic or load a short clip, then export the pack to share it with friends. A robot text-to-speech voice for unrecorded lines can be switched on there. Toggle music, sound effects and voices on the home screen, or press M in game to mute or unmute the music. Play my own music file lets you pick any audio file on your computer to loop instead of the built-in soundtrack.

Menus

A / D or arrows to choose · Space, Enter or click to confirm · Esc to go back.

Pause & key check

Press ESC during a fight to pause (on one keyboard, player 2 uses BACKSPACE). The pause screen lists every keybind with your character's actual move names, and lights up whatever key you press, so you can test your controls. Online, either player can pause, and it pauses for both.

Modes & online play

Game modes

  • Normal — 3 lives each, one continuous fight. When someone is KO'd, the winner keeps their health, position and cooldowns; the fallen fighter drops back in from the sky after 5 seconds with 5 seconds of invincibility (and no fall damage). First to lose all lives loses the match.
  • Endless — no lives. KOs add to a kill counter and the fighter respawns instantly.

Training (solo)

Press 🧪 Training on the home screen to test any fighter on your own. You use the full online layout (mouse + WASD + Q / E / R / F, block, dash, Maximum Output) and get a target that stands still, can't die, and heals back up 1.5s after you stop hitting it. Pick a map — including the Training Room, a flat floor with distance markers every 100px that only appears here — then your fighter. Training doesn't earn coins.

KeyOption
1Infinite meters — every super, special and domain / ultimate bar stays full.
2Infinite cursed energy, no cooldowns — every ability, Maximum Output move, super and domain only needs its own charge.
3Reset — positions, health, terrain.
4Switch to the next fighter on the spot.
5Switch between the online combat system and the classic local one.
0Hide the options bar.

The readout at the top shows your combo damage, hit count, last hit and best combo. ESC pauses as usual (controls, combat guide, your fighter's moves).

Playing online

  1. One player presses Host online game and gets a 5-letter code.
  2. The other types the code and presses Join — or opens the copied invite link.
  3. The host picks the mode and map; each player picks their own character.

Anyone else who joins with the same code watches as a spectator. The host's computer runs the match, so keep the host's tab visible.

If joining gets stuck

The join screen shows which step failed. "Can't reach the matchmaking server" usually means the network (often school Wi-Fi or a school laptop) is blocking it — try home Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot.

Local 2 player

Two people on one keyboard, using the original layout. No internet needed.

Combat basics

Melee combo

  • Each punch deals 2 and stuns briefly. Three hits fill your combo pips.
  • The 4th attack is a finisher: on the ground it deals 5 and knocks the opponent away; in the air it's a dive slam for 15.
  • Casting a domain spends the bar right away. For the first third of the hand sign you can be interrupted; after that you're untouchable until it opens. Once it's open you can be hit as normal (except Higuruma, who can't be hurt during his trial).
  • If your domain gets cancelled — the cast is interrupted, you lose a clash, it's shattered by the Inverted Spear, or you die mid-domain — you get 50% of the domain bar back.
  • Knocked-down fighters can't be hit until they get up, and they flicker with i-frames (can't be hit) for a moment after standing up and after respawning.
  • You can keep moving while you swing (you just can't turn around mid-punch).
  • Hold TAB during a fight to see both fighters' moves.
  • Playing online (separate computers)? Melee works differently: real combo strings, blocking, perfect blocks, dashes and Maximum Output (V). See Online Combat in the sidebar.

Health

  • Fall damage: a long drop costs a little health (1–8 HP, never lethal).
  • Regeneration: after 15 seconds without dealing or taking damage, you heal 2 HP every 3 seconds.
  • Crumbling terrain: cut a chunk loose (nothing holding it up) and it falls — it hurts anyone it lands on, then shatters. Broken terrain grows back after 30s.

Cursed energy

Every fighter has a cursed energy (CE) bar under their health bar that refills on its own, and moves spend it.

  • Q / E moves cost a set amount of CE (stronger moves cost more) and have a cooldown of 3/4 of what it used to be. If you can't afford one, its box goes dark and shows how much it needs.
  • Super (R): still needs its hit charge, and also 50% of your CE bar.
  • Domain: needs its charge and a full CE bar. Ultimates (fighters without a domain) need 75%. Both empty the bar, and it doesn't refill while your domain or ultimate is running. A cancelled domain gives back 50% of the domain bar and 50% of your CE.
  • Maximum Output (online V; one keyboard E / I; your aura lights up while it's on): ability 1 / 2 fire their Maximum Output versions for about twice the CE. Your super and domain still work. Only one Maximum Output move per fighter can be blocked; the other — and every super and ultimate — can only be countered with a perfect block.
  • Steering, detonating or swapping with something you already have out (Lapse Blue's orb, Convergence, the puppet, Ui Ui, the crow) is free.
  • Black Flash (Yuji, Todo, Mahito): your CE refills 250% faster for 10 seconds afterwards.
  • Choso can keep going when he's out of CE: he pays with his own blood (1 HP = 3 CE, never below 1 HP) and leaves a blood pool, which feeds his Supernova.
  • Hakari's jackpot gives him infinite cursed energy. The Inverted Spear of Heaven drains 30 CE per hit. Upgrades: Six Eyes and Cursed Energy Flow refill it faster.

★ = special grade (sorcerer or curse): much bigger pools. Yuta and Mechamaru have by far the biggest reserves; Gojo (Six Eyes) and Sukuna refill several times faster than anyone else; Takaba has the smallest pool. Moves are expensive — a normal fighter can only fire two or three in a row.

Charge meters

  • Super (Fuga, Hollow Purple, Copy, Puppet, Imaginary Brother, Slicing Exorcism) — usually 40 damage dealt, plus 50% CE.
  • Domain / ultimate — 150 damage dealt. Only one domain can be open at a time.
  • Domain clash: if your opponent's domain is open and yours is charged, cast it anyway. Both fighters freeze and get key prompts; every correct key pushes the clash line toward the other side, and a wrong key stalls you briefly. Push it all the way, or be ahead when the 6s run out, to win. If the challenger wins, their domain replaces the old one. If the defender wins, their domain stays (+1.5s) and the challenger's charge is spent. Works between Sukuna, Gojo, Yuta and Higuruma.
  • Yuji's ultimate uses its own 100-damage meter.

Domains

On the big maps a domain opens a screen-sized arena around its caster and pulls the opponent in. Anti-domain techniques (online: hold click + F, for fighters who have one) block domain sure-hits, and the Inverted Spear of Heaven shatters a domain on hit.

Maps & terrain

Shibuya Station

The Shibuya Incident, top to bottom: the street under the Veil (scramble crossing, Hachikō, the JR platform with a train on top, the QFRONT-style building and 109), the B1 concourse, the B3 transfer level (with the restroom where Yuji fought Choso), and the B5F Fukutoshin line platform with the tunnel to Meiji-jingumae. Each floor has openings with ledges to climb or drop through.

Sister School Exchange

Tokyo Jujutsu High in daylight: the tall main building with stairwells, a stone terrace with a climbable three-storey pagoda, a white-walled hall, the campus wall, a grey stone torii, and a cedar forest you can climb branch to branch.

Shinjuku

The showdown. On the left, the intact Nishi-Shinjuku street — glass towers with fire-escape ledges and lobbies, and an elevated road with its middle span collapsed. On the right, the rubble field: tilted slabs, sheared tower stumps, and a tall broken tower.

Terrain rules

  • Almost every technique carves holes that match its shape. Broken terrain returns after 30 seconds (it waits if someone is standing there).
  • Wooden platforms, ledges, tree trunks, posts and support columns are one-way: walk through them, jump up through them, stand on top. Hold down to drop through.
  • Stone, brick, glass, metal and roofs are solid.

Items

Cursed tools appear every 26 seconds (at most 2 at once), often on rooftops and ledges. Stand on one and press G. You can carry one at a time; your HUD shows it and its timer.

A disaster curse of the forest. She chokes off your cursed energy, roots you in place and turns the whole arena into a tangle of roots.

KeyMoveDetails
QCursed BudsThrows 3 arcing seeds (hold down or up to throw them low or high). Each one that lands deals 5 damage and drains about 17% of the opponent's ultimate / domain bar. 56 CE, 5.2s cooldown.
EFlower FieldA field of flowers blooms on the ground in front of her for 4 seconds. Anyone standing in it is stunned briefly and takes 7 damage (once every 1.5s). 72 CE, 6.8s cooldown.
RRoot Grab (super, 35)Aim with up / down, then a root lashes out up to 440px. If it catches the opponent it drags them right up to Hanami: 10 damage and a short stun.
FRoot Rampage (ultimate, 150)For 15 seconds a giant root bursts out and follows your mouse (online, your own mouse). The tip hits for 8 and knocks people around. Everything it grows through becomes a root platform anyone can stand on. The roots wither shortly after it ends. Without a mouse over the game, the root hunts the opponent on its own.
MovementNature's SpringJumps 10% higher.
Click + F (online)Domain AmplificationLike she used against Gojo in Shibuya: 5s of immunity to domain sure-hits and 30% less damage taken, but no abilities while it's up. Press again to drop it early. 80 CE, 15s cooldown.

Mahito

A special-grade curse who can touch the soul itself. He reshapes his own body and his opponent's, and is very hard to pin down.

KeyMoveDetails
QIdle TransfigurationA short-range palm strike: 12 damage and a brief stun. The target is reshaped for 5 seconds: 30% slower and takes 20% more damage from everything. 48 CE, 4.5s cooldown.
EPolymorphic Soul IsomerReleases a transfigured human that runs along the ground toward the opponent and explodes on contact (or after ~4s, or at a wall): 16 damage and a knockback in a wide blast. 64 CE, 6s cooldown.
RInstant Spirit Body of Distorted Killing (super, 45)8 seconds in his killing form: blade arm and spines, 25% faster, deals 40% more damage and takes 30% less.
FSelf-Embodiment of Perfection (domain, 150)Giant stitched hands close in from every side. The sure-hit touch deals 6 damage every 1.1s and keeps the opponent reshaped. Can clash with other domains.
MovementSoul MalleabilityWalks straight through thin walls (up to ~6 cells thick). After 4 seconds without being hit, regenerates 1 HP every 0.7s.

Takaba

A comedian whose technique, Comedian, makes whatever he finds funny come true. As long as he thinks it's funny, it works.

KeyMoveDetails
QRock Paper ScissorsBoth fighters freeze and get 1.8s to throw Rock / Paper / Scissors with their own Q / E / R (local: 1 2 3 and J K L). No pick = random. The loser takes 30 damage and gets launched — even if that's Takaba. A draw halves the cooldown. 80 CE, 9s cooldown.
E1000 Years of DeathTeleports behind the opponent (within 460px) and delivers the infamous poke: 14 damage and a big launch forward. 72 CE, 6.8s cooldown.
RCounter (super, 25)A 0.45s stance. If anything hits him during it, he takes no damage at all, gets brief invincibility, and a nearby attacker is stunned. Time it right as their attack lands.
FThe Truck (ultimate, 150)HONK HONK. After a short warning a giant truck drives across the whole map in the opponent's lane, through everything — terrain, puppets, people: 45 damage and a massive launch. Jump to dodge it.
MovementComedian12% of hits on him turn into a gag: no damage, just a slide whistle.

Naoya Zen'in

Heir of the Zen'in clan. Projection Sorcery splits a second into 24 frames: he moves along a motion he's already drawn, faster than anyone — and anyone who can't follow 24 fps gets frozen in a frame. He has 4 lives with 75 HP each; the last one he spends as a vengeful cursed spirit with new moves and a domain.

KeyMoveDetails
QProjection DashRuns forward at full speed and punches the first fighter in his way: 14 damage and a knockback. 40 CE, 3.8s cooldown.
EFrame BarrageHand on his head, eyes closed, not even looking: four backhands a frame apart (3 each), then a launching kick (9). 48 CE, 4.5s cooldown.
R24 FPS (super, 40)Both fighters freeze. Naoya draws a motion with his movement keys and attack — 12 keys on one keyboard, 24 online. Then the opponent has to press the same keys in order. One wrong key (or running out of time) and they're frozen in a frame for 8 seconds: they can't move and take 14% more damage. If they keep up, Naoya is the one frozen, for 1.5s. Needs 50% CE.
F—No domain while human. His 4th (last) life is spent as a cursed spirit.
MovementProjection SorceryThe fastest fighter (28% faster, building up to 50% after a second of running), but jumps 10% lower and deals 10% less damage. Every 3rd hit of a quick string freezes the target in a frame for 0.6s (at most once every 3s) — a free link into the next hit. To stop wall loops, his damage falls off within one string: half after 25 damage, a fifth after 40. But Projection Sorcery has a rule: if Naoya whiffs Projection Dash, Frame Barrage or one of his Maximum Output moves, he breaks his own 24 fps motion and is frozen in a frame for 1s (taking 14% more damage).

Vengeful Cursed Spirit (4th life)

When Naoya drops to his last life he comes back as the cursed spirit he became after death: a skull-faced white shell. Pool grows to 220 CE (special grade). Endless mode: after he's been killed three times.

KeyMoveDetails
QRocketTurns into a rocket for 2.4s that you steer with the movement keys. Smashes straight through terrain; 20 damage per hit; press Q again to blow up early (8 more around you). 64 CE, 6s cooldown.
EFrame FieldFive frames in a row in front of him for 6s. Anyone who walks into one is caught in it. Press E again to detonate them all: 10 each, and 22 to anyone caught. 56 CE, 5.3s cooldown.
R24 FPS (super, 40)Same frame prompt as before.
FTime Cell Moon Palace (domain, 150)A black void with a white road winding up to a towering cluster of cells crowned by a giant eye. Projection Sorcery is applied to the target's cells: every motion that breaks 24 fps tears them apart — 2 damage every 0.25s while they move, attack or fall. Standing still is safe. Naoya is 20% faster inside. Needs a full CE bar.
